summary.headline: Shalby Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.6% YoY to ₹338.6 cr, but EBITDA was flat at ₹49 cr and margin fell to 14.5% from 16%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11.6% YoY to ₹338.6 cr while EBITDA was nearly flat at ₹49 cr, pulling margin down about 150 bps to 14.5%. Consolidated PAT rose to ₹10.5 cr from ₹7.7 cr, helped by a lower group tax rate, though PBT fell to ₹19.7 cr from ₹22.7 cr. Hospitals grew revenue about 7% but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 18.4% from 21.6%, while MedTech revenue (about ₹47 cr) and India entity revenue (about ₹36 cr) grew sharply and consolidated MedTech EBITDA turned positive for a fourth straight quarter. Management guided to hospital margins of up to 20% for the full year and to double-digit MedTech EBITDA margins, with both reliant on items not yet visible in the numbers.

segments.name: Hospitals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹259 cr (+7% YoY), EBITDA ₹47.8 cr at 18.4% margin vs 21.6%. Occupied beds 701 (+9.8% YoY), occupancy 51%, ARPOB ₹44,711 (vs ₹45,673), ALOS 3.69 days (vs 3.53).

segments.name: Shalby International (Gurgaon)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹26.2 cr (vs ₹23.2 cr YoY), ARPOB ₹91,326, ALOS 3.8 days. Achieved first EBITDA break-even since acquisition, reported at about 7% EBITDA margin; occupancy about 24% per analyst question.

segments.name: MedTech – SMTL India
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹36 cr per call (+29% QoQ, +98% YoY); management also cited India revenue growth of over 100% in volumes. Figures in the call are inconsistent (₹22.9 cr cited elsewhere).

segments.name: MedTech – US (SATUS)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹38.8 cr with about 9% sequential growth; standalone EBITDA marginally negative. US volumes flat YoY; FX headwind cited.

segments.name: MedTech – Singapore (SGTPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹9.9 million, lower sequentially; EBITDA about ₹5.8 million, a significant improvement vs prior quarters.

guidance_outlook: Hospital EBITDA margin: management is 'strongly confident' of reaching up to 20% for the full year FY27.
Gross margin expected to rise 100–200 bps each quarter going forward.

MedTech: double-digit EBITDA margin expected after US cost initiatives; half of progress made, remainder expected over the next 6 months. Monthly cash burn to fall ~₹3 cr/month from initiatives done in Q1 and a further ~₹3 cr/month once a project is implemented by Q4 FY27.
Shalby International occupancy expected to reach ~30% from Q3 or Q4 FY27; PBT break-even targeted around Q3–Q4 FY27 (6–9 months).
Group ROCE, currently ~7% (standalone ~9.5%), expected to reach 11–13% in 1–2 years.
Gurgaon unit to pay no tax for next 2–3 years due to carried-forward losses. Hospital tax rate moved to ~26% from 35%.
Inventory holding days expected to improve about 30%.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of about ₹160 cr in recent years, including bunker facility, robotics and MedTech investments; management expects minimal capex in the current and next year.
Bunkers (radiation facilities) installed in units last year; activation in Q1 with further uptick expected in Q2, including government-scheme coverage for bunker treatments.

Mumbai expansion: 200-bed greenfield Asha Parekh Hospital project; discussions ongoing with trustees, no approval yet. Funding by debt or internal accruals to be decided; no further debt for hospitals or MedTech expected.
47 transplants in Q1 (41 kidney, 5 liver, 1 bone marrow); liver transplant and KTP doctors recently replaced, full effect expected from Q2.
demand_pricing: Government share of payer mix rose to 32% from 24% a year ago; mix now 30% self-pay, 38% insurance, 32% government. Management cited a super-specialty rate win at Krishna unit.
TPA renewals underway, with management expecting a 5–7% revenue uplift from renewals and tie-ups in discussion.
Units Krishna, Mohali and Naroda grew ~30% YoY; Surat and Indore underperformed and are recruiting doctors.
International revenue ~42% of Shalby International operating revenue; group international business ~₹13 cr (₹2 cr Gurgaon, ₹11 cr other units).
Consolidated revenue of ₹923 mn in FY25, ₹1.3 bn in FY26, ₹472 mn in Q1 FY27 (MedTech-related, as stated).

qa_highlights.question: Rajakumar (RK Invest): Will hospital margins sustain or improve from here, with no one-offs or headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to improve, citing bunker activation in Q1 with further uptick in Q2, TPA renewals with a potential 5-7% revenue uplift, Gurgaon EBITDA turning positive, and recovery in Krishna, Mohali and Naroda (~30% YoY growth), while Surat and Indore are recruiting doctors.

qa_highlights.question: Rajakumar: Why has the implants/MedTech bottom line deteriorated despite revenue rising from ₹28 cr to ₹42 cr, and why did losses widen from ₹7.4 cr in Q4 to ₹11.4 cr in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher interest and full-year depreciation from earlier capex, and said Q4 had a forex gain that did not recur in Q1; gross margin is expected to rise 100-200 bps each quarter. Deferred tax asset is not recognised on US MedTech losses on a conservative basis and will be reconsidered when profitability improves.

qa_highlights.question: Kashish Thakur (Elara): What is driving weak MedTech profitability, especially in the US, and when can sustainable double-digit EBITDA margins come?
qa_highlights.answer: Shanay Shah cited FX (USD/INR) as a major factor, India volumes up over 100%, US volumes flat. Cost initiatives cut cash burn by about ₹3 cr/month, with a further ₹3 cr/month once a project is implemented by Q4 FY27; half the progress is done and the rest is expected over the next 6 months, given 6-9 months to 1 year for US FDA-related changes.

qa_highlights.question: Kashish Thakur: Hospital standalone margin fell ~320 bps to 18.4% despite occupancy at 51%; can FY27 margin guidance be reinstated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to new doctors and specialties taking about a quarter to mature, with TPA renewals and bunker revenue flowing into next quarter. It is 'strongly confident' of an EBITDA margin of up to 20% for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Kashish Thakur: Shalby International occupancy is 24% yet EBITDA-positive; what are the occupancy, margin and breakeven aspirations?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy expected to reach about 30% from Q3 or Q4 FY27, with PBT-positive targeted around Q3 to Q4, within 6-9 months; the unit posted about a 7% EBITDA margin in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Kashish Thakur: Tax rate guidance for FY27, and ROCE levers and timelines, plus status of the Mumbai expansion.
qa_highlights.answer: Hospital tax rate moved to about 26% from 35%, a permanent benefit; group ETR fell to 47% from 66%. Gurgaon will pay no tax for 2-3 years on carried-forward losses. Group ROCE is about 7% (standalone 9.5%), expected to reach 11-13% in 1-2 years with minimal capex. Mumbai talks with trustees are ongoing with no approval yet.

qa_highlights.question: Tripti Shukla (Kedia Securities): Why did ICRA downgrade the rating from A+ to A on the ₹830 cr facility, and how is debt being managed given the ₹129 cr Kotak working capital facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the rating move procedural, with outlook revised to stable from negative and possible re-evaluation later. The Kotak facility is a replacement of existing debt at about 30 bps lower cost, not fresh debt; net debt is expected flat to lower.

qa_highlights.question: Tripti Shukla: Is the rise in government payer mix (32% vs 24%) a temporary shift or a volume strategy, and how is the cash conversion cycle protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher government share follows rate renewals, including a super-specialty rate win at Krishna; bunker treatments are expected to be covered under government schemes. Receivables are being managed with automated recovery tools, bill-submission follow-up and regular visits to government offices.

qa_highlights.question: Tripti Shukla: Expected cash capex for the 200-bed Mumbai (Asha Parekh) project, and how will it be balanced against ROCE goals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a greenfield project and may need a different ROCE benchmark once finalised. No further debt is expected for hospitals or MedTech; funding via debt or internal accruals will be decided later, with no capex figure given.

risks_watch: MedTech: whether the consolidated EBITDA stays positive beyond a fourth quarter and whether the double-digit margin target (half progress made, rest over 6 months) is delivered, given US FX and flat US volumes.
Hospital standalone margin recovery toward 20% full-year guidance from 18.4% in Q1, which depends on doctor ramp-up, TPA renewals and bunker revenue not yet visible in the numbers.
Rating: ICRA cut the long-term rating to A from A+ (outlook stable); the company said it could be re-evaluated in coming quarters.
Rising government payer mix (32% from 24%) at lower ARPOB (₹44,711 vs ₹45,673) raises receivables and cash conversion risk.
Mumbai 200-bed greenfield project: trustee approval pending, funding and capex amount undecided, with implications for group ROCE.
Data inconsistencies in the call: India MedTech revenue cited as ~₹36 cr and ~₹22.9 cr, and the MedTech EBITDA figure given as ~₹1.7 million and ~1.6 million; reconcile against the filed results.
key_quotes: We are strongly confident as per our estimate to see EBITDA margin of upward to 20% on to the whole year basis.
So this is all underway and half of the progress is already made the other half is expected in the next 6 months from here on.
This is not an increase in the debt level, this is just a replacement.

We do not see our bottom line to worsen off from here rather we are confident to see a better bottom line in the subsequent quarter also importantly by the reason of the upside on to our gross margins which is expected to increase about 100 basis to 200 basis points each quarter from here on.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and forward-leaning on hospital margins, MedTech profitability and Shalby International breakeven, repeatedly giving timelines and targets. It was more evasive when pressed on the sharp MedTech and bottom-line losses, the Q4-to-Q1 PAT swing, and the ICRA rating cut, attributing these to FX, one-offs and procedural factors. Several answers were repetitive and unclear in the transcript.
